newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Guinea-Bissau civil servants strike again.
newsitem.headline: Guinea-Bissau civil servants strike again.

text.p: Guinea-Bissau's 12,000 civil servants started a four-day strike for higher pay on Tuesday, saying the country's new currency had pushed up inflation.
"The country is paralysed 95 percent. Next time it will be 100 percent," Desejado Lima Dacosta, leader of the civil service union, told Reuters in neighbouring Senegal by phone.

Guinea-Bissau civil servants went on strike earlier this month after the country became a full member of the West African Monetary Union (UMOA) on August 1 and its currency, the peso, was abandoned for the Franc Zone's CFA franc.
Lima Dacosta claimed that since Guinea-Bissau joined the Franc Zone "inflation has risen to 56 percent".
Up-to-date official statistics were not available.

Officials at the regional central bank, the BCEAO, based in Dakar, dismissed any link between the currency change and inflation. They say limited price rises in recent weeks were due to seasonal factors.
Lima Dacosta said his members had the lowest salaries of any civil servants in Africa.
"We have salaries of 10,000 CFA francs or even 9,000 ($15 per month)," one unionist said.
Guinea-Bissau officials said they could consider raising salaries because of the constraints of World Bank and International Monetary Fund adjustment programmes. ($1 = 620 CFA francs)
